book_name: 动词的过去式和过去分词

words.tr:
n. 熊；
v. 承受；忍受；带有；生（孩子）；
words.ex: A bear walked near the campsite.
words.ex_cn: 一只熊在露营地附近走动。
words.en: If you bear something, you accept it and are able to deal with it, even though it is unpleasant or painful. A bear is a large, strong wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

words.tr: adj. 出生的；天生的； v. 生（孩子）；“bear”的过去分词；
words.ex: He is a born teacher.
words.en: When a baby is born, it comes out of its mother's body at the beginning of its life.

words.tr:
v. 打；敲打；击败；
n. 一击；跳动；
words.ex: He beat the drum loudly.
words.en: To defeat someone in a game, competition, election, or battle; to hit someone or something many times with your hand, a stick, etc.

words.tr: adj. 被踩实的； v. “beat”的过去分词；
words.ex: The beaten path through the forest was easy to walk on.
words.ex_cn: 穿过森林的被踩实的小路很容易走。
words.en: If someone is beaten in a game, competition, election, or battle, they are defeated by their opponents.

words.tr: v. 变成；成为；变得；
words.ex: The caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
words.en: To begin to be something or to develop into something.

words.tr: v. 变成；成为；变得；“become”的过去式；
words.ex: He became a teacher after graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他毕业后成为一名老师。
words.en: the past tense of 'become', which means to begin to be something

words.tr: v. 开始；着手；
words.ex: He begins his homework after dinner.
words.en: To start doing something; to take the first step into a process or activity.

words.tr: v. 开始；“begin”的过去分词；
words.ex: The meeting has begun.
words.en: Past participle of begin: to start doing something.

words.tr: v. 开始；创建；“begin”的过去式；
words.ex: He began to walk to school.
words.en: Began is the past tense of begin. To begin means to start doing something.

words.tr:
v. 吹；打击；
n. 打击；
words.ex: The wind blows the leaves away.
words.en: To move air or gas forcefully; to strike something with force.

words.tr: v. 吹；刮风；浪费；“blow” 的过去式
words.ex: He blew out the candles on his cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吹灭了蛋糕上的蜡烛。
words.en: To blow means to move air or to cause air to move, especially in a way that is noticeable or strong.

words.tr: v. 吹；“blow”的过去分词； adj. 胀起的；
words.ex: The wind blew the leaves away.
words.en: Blown refers to something that has been shaped by blowing, especially glass, or to the state of being swollen or out of breath.

words.tr:
v. 打破；打断；
n. 休息；中断；破裂；
words.ex: He broke the glass by accident.
words.en: If you break something, you cause it to separate into two or more pieces, often in a way that is irreparable.

words.tr: v. 打破；打断；“break”的过去式； adj. 破产的；身无分文的；
words.ex: He broke the glass by accident.
words.en: If you are broke, you have no money.

words.tr: adj. 破损的；弄坏的； v. 打破；打断；“break”的过去分词；
words.ex: The broken cup lay on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 破了的杯子躺在地板上。
words.en: Damaged or shattered into pieces, typically as a result of force or impact.

words.tr: v. 带来；引起；
words.ex: He brings his lunch to work every day.
words.en: To bring something means to carry or convey it to the place where you are or to the place you are talking about.

words.tr: v. 带来；引起；导致；“bring”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He brought a book to class.
words.en: To take or carry someone or something to a place or a person, or in the direction of the person speaking.

words.tr:
v. 建筑；建造；逐步加强；
n. 体格；体形；
words.ex: They build a house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他们在湖边建了一所房子。
words.en: To construct something by putting parts or material together.

words.tr: v. 建筑；建造；“build”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: They built a house last year.
words.ex_cn: 他们去年建了一栋房子。
words.en: The past tense and past participle of 'build', meaning to construct something by putting parts or material together.

words.tr: v. 燃烧；烧伤；
words.ex: The wood burns slowly in the fire.
words.en: If there is a fire or a flame somewhere, you say that there is a burn there. When you burn something, you destroy or damage it with fire or heat.

words.tr: v. 燃烧；烧伤；“burn”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The wood burnt in the fire.
words.en: Damaged or injured by fire or heat.

words.tr: v. 买；换取；相信；
words.ex: I buy apples at the market.
words.en: To buy means to obtain something by paying money for it.

words.tr: v. 买；“buy”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I bought a book yesterday.
words.en: The past tense and past participle of buy, meaning to acquire something by paying for it.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；赶上；理解；得病；接住；
n. 接住；搭扣；
words.ex: He tried to catch the ball.
words.en: If you catch something or someone, you manage to get hold of them or stop them from moving, often after a chase or search.

words.tr: v. 抓住；赶上；“catch”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The boy caught a fish in the river.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在河里抓到了一条鱼。
words.en: Caught is the past tense and past participle of catch, which means to seize or capture something or someone.

words.tr: v. 选择
words.ex: He chooses coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都选择喝咖啡。
words.en: To choose means to select someone or something from a group of possibilities.

words.tr: v. 选择；“choose”的过去式；
words.ex: He chose the red shirt.
words.en: If you choose someone or something from several people or things that are available, you decide which person or thing you want to have.

words.tr: v. 选择；“choose”的过去分词； adj. 挑选出来的；
words.ex: He was chosen as the team captain.
words.en: Having been selected as the best or most suitable.

words.tr: v. 来；到来；
words.ex: Please come to my house tomorrow.
words.en: To move or travel towards the speaker or with the speaker; to arrive at a place; to happen or take place.

words.tr: v. 来；来到；“come”的过去式；
words.ex: He came to school yesterday.
words.en: The past tense of come, meaning to move or travel towards the speaker or with the speaker.

words.tr:
n. 费用；代价；
v. 花费；
words.ex: The cost of the book is ten dollars.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的费用是十美元。
words.en: The amount of money that you need in order to buy, make, or do something.

words.tr:
v. 切；割；削减；
n. 切；割；削减；
words.ex: He cut the apple with a knife.
words.en: To make an opening, incision, or wound in (something) with a sharp-edged tool or object.

words.tr:
v. 处理；对付；交易；
n. 交易；协议；
words.ex: He can deal with difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理困难的问题。
words.en: A deal is an agreement or arrangement, especially in business or politics, that is beneficial to all the parties involved.

words.tr: v. 处理；“deal”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He dealt with the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速处理了这个问题。
words.en: If you deal with a particular person or organization, you have business or social contact with them.

words.tr: v. 挖；掘；
words.ex: He dig a hole in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里挖了一个洞。
words.en: To dig means to break up, turn over, or remove earth, sand, etc., using a tool, a machine, or your hands. It can also mean to search for something by moving or looking through something, or to like or enjoy something very much.

words.tr: v. 挖；翻土；“dig”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He dug a hole in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里挖了一个洞。
words.en: To dig means to break up, turn over, or remove earth, sand, etc., with a tool or machine, or with hands, paws, snout, etc.

words.tr: v. 做
words.ex: I do my homework every evening.
words.en: To perform or accomplish something

words.tr: v. 做；“do”的过去式；
words.ex: He did his homework after dinner.
words.en: Did is the past tense of do.

words.tr: v. 完成；“do”的过去分词； adj. 已完成的；
words.ex: I done my homework.
words.en: If something is done, it has been completed or finished.

words.tr: v. 提取；画；吸引；拉；
words.ex: I draw money from the bank every week.
words.en: To make a picture, pattern, or diagram by making lines and marks, especially with a pen or pencil, on paper.

words.tr: v. 画；提取；吸引；“draw”的过去式；
words.ex: He drew a cat on the paper.
words.en: Drew is the past tense of draw, which means to produce a picture or diagram by making lines and marks on paper or another surface.

words.tr: v. 吸引；"draw"的过去分词；画；拉；提取；“draw”的过去分词；
words.ex: The bright colors drawn the children's attention.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引了孩子们的注意。
words.en: If someone looks drawn, their face is thin and they look very tired, ill, worried, or unhappy.

words.tr:
n. 梦；梦想；
v. 梦想；做梦；
words.ex: I had a strange dream last night.
words.ex_cn: 我昨晚做了一个奇怪的梦。
words.en: A dream is a series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep. It can also refer to a cherished aspiration, ambition, or ideal.

words.tr: v. 梦；“dream”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I dreamt of flying last night.
words.ex_cn: 我昨晚梦见自己在飞翔。
words.en: Dreamt is the past tense and past participle of dream, which means to experience thoughts, images, or emotions while sleeping.

words.tr:
n. 饮料；酒；
v. 喝；喝酒；
words.ex: I bought a cold drink at the store.
words.ex_cn: 我在商店买了一瓶冷饮。
words.en: To take liquid into the mouth and swallow it; a liquid that can be swallowed as refreshment or nourishment.

words.tr: v. 喝；“drink”的过去式；
words.ex: He drank water after running.
words.en: The past tense of 'drink', meaning to take liquid into the mouth and swallow it.

words.tr: v. 喝；喝酒；“drink”的过去分词； adj. 喝醉的；
words.ex: He has drunk all the water.
words.en: If someone is drunk, they have consumed so much alcohol that it has affected their ability to think and speak clearly.

words.tr:
v. 驾驶；驱使；
n. 动力；
words.ex: He drives a car to work every day.
words.en: To operate and control the direction and speed of a motor vehicle; to push, propel, or carry along forcibly or strongly.

words.tr: v. 驱使；驾驶；“drive”的过去式；
words.ex: Fear drove him to leave the city.
words.ex_cn: 恐惧驱使他离开了这座城市。
words.en: A drove is a large group of animals, especially cattle or sheep, moving together. As a verb, it is the past tense of drive, meaning to force animals or people to move in a particular direction.

words.tr: v. 驱使；驾驶；“drive”的过去分词； adj. 发愤图强的；
words.ex: Fear of failure drove him to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 对失败的恐惧驱使他更加努力工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as driven, you mean they are very strongly motivated to achieve something or to do something.

words.tr: v. 吃
words.ex: He eats an apple every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一个苹果。
words.en: To consume food, typically as a regular part of one's diet.

words.tr: v. 吃；“eat”的过去式；
words.ex: He ate an apple for breakfast.
words.en: the past tense of eat, which means to consume food

words.tr: v. 吃；“eat”的过去分词；
words.ex: The dog has eaten all the food.
words.ex_cn: 狗已经把所有食物吃光了。
words.en: The past participle of 'eat', used to describe something that has been consumed.

words.tr:
v. 下降；跌倒；
n. 落下；跌落；秋天；
words.ex: The temperature falls quickly at night.
words.en: To move downward, typically rapidly and freely without control, from a higher to a lower level.

words.tr: v. 跌倒；下降；砍伐；“fall”的过去式；
words.ex: He fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔了下来。
words.en: To cut down (a tree); to knock down (a person or animal); the skin of an animal with the hair or wool still on it; fierce or cruel.

words.tr: v. 下降；跌倒；“fall”的过去分词； adj. 落下的；
words.ex: The leaf fallen from the tree.
words.en: Having dropped or come down from a higher place, often used to describe leaves, snow, or someone's moral state.

words.tr:
v. 喂；吃；
n. 饲养；喂养；
words.ex: She feeds the cat every morning.
words.en: To give food to a person or an animal; to supply something to a machine or a system.

words.tr: v. 喂；吃；“feed”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She fed the cat every morning.
words.en: To provide food for someone or something, or to give someone or something the necessary materials or resources for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adv. 真正地；非常地；
words.ex: He really loves his job.
words.ex_cn: 他真正地热爱他的工作。
words.en: You use really to emphasize that something is true or that it is the case.

words.tr: v. 感到；认为；“feel”的过去式和过去分词； n. 毛毡；毡制品；
words.ex: I felt happy when I saw my friend.
words.ex_cn: 当我见到我的朋友时，我感到开心。
words.en: If you feel a particular emotion or physical sensation, you experience it.

words.tr:
v. 打架；战斗；
n. 打架；战斗；
words.ex: The two boys fight every day after school.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天放学后都打架。
words.en: To fight means to take part in a violent struggle involving the exchange of physical blows or the use of weapons. It can also refer to a determined effort to achieve or resist something.

words.tr: v. 战斗；打架；争论；“fight”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: They fought in the war last year.
words.ex_cn: 他们去年在战争中战斗。
words.en: Fought is the past tense and past participle of fight. To fight means to take part in a violent struggle involving the exchange of physical blows or the use of weapons.

words.tr: n. 鳍；
words.ex: The fish swam fast using its fin.
words.en: A fin is a thin flat part that sticks out from the body of a fish, used for swimming and balancing.

words.tr: v. 发现；找到；建立；认为；“find”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He found a strange stone on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩上发现了一块奇怪的石头。
words.en: To establish or set up (an organization, institution, or place) on a firm or permanent basis.

words.tr:
v. 飞翔；飞行；
n. 苍蝇；
words.ex: Birds fly in the sky.
words.en: To move through the air using wings; or a small insect with two wings.

words.tr: v. 飞翔；飞行；“fly”的过去式；
words.ex: The bird flew over the tree.
words.en: Flew is the past tense of fly, which means to move through the air using wings.

words.tr: v. 飞；坐飞机；“fly”的过去分词；
words.ex: The bird has flown away.
words.en: Flown is the past participle of fly, meaning to move through the air using wings.

words.tr: v. 忘记；遗忘；
words.ex: I forget where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you forget something, you fail to remember it.

words.tr: v. 忘记；遗忘；“forget”的过去式；
words.ex: I forgot my keys at home.
words.en: If you forget something, you do not remember it.

words.tr: v. 忘记；“forget”的过去分词； adj. 被忘却的；
words.ex: The keys were forgotten on the table.
words.en: If something is forgotten, it has been left behind or not remembered by someone.

words.tr: v. 得到；获得；使；变得；收到；
words.ex: I got a new book from the library.
words.ex_cn: 我从图书馆得到了一本新书。
words.en: To come into possession of something; to receive or be given something.

words.tr: v. 得到；明白；获得；“get”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I got a gift from my friend.
words.ex_cn: 我从朋友那里得到了一份礼物。
words.en: Got is the past tense and past participle of get, which means to come into possession of something, to receive something, or to obtain something.

words.tr: v. 给予；发出；
words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.en: To freely transfer the possession of something to someone; to cause or allow someone to have something.

words.tr: v. 给予；发出；“give”的过去式；
words.ex: She gave me a book.
words.en: Past tense of give, which means to freely transfer the possession of something to someone.

words.tr: v. 走；去
words.ex: He goes to school every day.
words.en: To move or travel from one place to another.

words.tr: v. 走；进行；“go”的过去式；
words.ex: He went to the store yesterday.
words.en: Went is the past tense of go.

words.tr: v. 去；走；“go”的过去分词； adj. 已往的；离去的；死去的；
words.ex: He is gone to the store.
words.en: No longer present; departed.

words.tr: v. 生长；成长；渐渐变成；种植；
words.ex: The plant grows quickly in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物在春天长得很快。
words.en: If someone or something grows, they increase in size, amount, or degree, often over a period of time.

words.tr: v. 成长；种植；养成；变得；“grow”的过去式；
words.ex: The tree grew tall near the house.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在房子附近长高了。
words.en: Grew is the past tense of grow, which means to increase in size or amount, or to become something different.

words.tr: v. 种植；成长；渐渐变成；生长；“grow”的过去分词； adj. 成熟的；成年的；长大的；
words.ex: He grown tomatoes in his garden.
words.en: Having reached maturity or full development; adult.

words.tr:
v. 悬挂；吊；
n. 悬挂；
words.ex: He hangs a picture on the wall.
words.en: To hang something means to attach it to something else so that it is supported from above and does not touch the ground.

words.tr: v. 悬挂；“hang”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He hung the picture on the wall.
words.en: to suspend or be suspended from above with the lower part dangling free

words.tr: v. 有；拥有；具有；经历；遭受；吃；喝；进行；完成；处于某种状态；认为；相信；主张；需要；应该；必须
words.ex: He has a book on algebra.
words.ex_cn: 他有一本关于代数的书。
words.en: A verb used to indicate possession, obligation, or experience; the third-person singular present form is 'has'.

words.tr: v. 有；吃；“have”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She had a book on the table.
words.en: Had is the past tense and past participle of have.

words.tr: v. 听；听见；
words.ex: I hear birds singing in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 我听到早晨鸟儿在唱歌。
words.en: To perceive or become aware of (sound) through the ear.

words.tr: v. 听；听见；“hear”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I heard a bird singing outside.
words.ex_cn: 我听到外面有一只鸟在唱歌。
words.en: To perceive or become aware of (sound) by the ear.

words.tr:
v. 隐藏；躲藏；
n. 兽皮；
words.ex: He hides the key under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 他把钥匙藏在垫子下面。
words.en: To conceal something or someone from view or discovery.

words.tr: v. 藏；“hide”的过去式；
words.ex: He hid the key under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 他把钥匙藏在门垫下面。
words.en: to put or keep out of sight; to prevent from being seen or discovered.

words.tr: adj. 隐藏的； v. 隐藏；“hide”的过去分词；
words.ex: The keys are hidden under the mat.
words.en: If something is hidden, it is not easily noticed or found.

words.tr:
v. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；抨击；达到；
n. 打；击；碰撞；袭击；(演出等)成功；
words.ex: He hit the ball with a bat.
words.en: If you hit someone or something, you deliberately touch them with a lot of force, with your hand or an object held in your hand.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；持有；容纳；保留；举行；
n. 拿；控制；持；
words.ex: He held the rope tightly.
words.en: To have or keep in the hand; to maintain in a grasp; to keep in a specified state, relation, or position; to contain or be capable of containing; to have in one's possession; to keep back from action; to delay the action or effect of; to keep in custody; to bear, sustain, or support; to have or maintain in the mind; to consider or esteem; to assert or affirm; to organize and carry on; to have the ownership or use of; to keep from falling or moving; to remain unbroken or unyielding; to remain attached or faithful; to remain valid or effective.

words.tr: v. 举行；持有；抓住；保存；容纳；“hold”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The school held a science fair last week.
words.ex_cn: 学校上周举行了一场科学展览会。
words.en: To have or keep in the hand; keep fast; grasp; to have or possess, as something in one's power or control.

words.tr: v. 受伤；
words.ex: He hurt his leg while playing soccer.
words.en: If you hurt someone, you cause them to feel pain. If you hurt a part of your body, you feel pain there. If someone is hurt, they are injured.

words.tr: v. 保持；保留；继续；
words.ex: She keeps the room clean every day.
words.en: To continue to have or hold something; to maintain a condition or position.

words.tr: v. 保持；保管；“keep”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She kept the room clean every day.
words.en: Kept is the past tense and past participle of keep. To keep something means to have it or continue to have it in your possession, or to store it somewhere because you might need it later.

words.tr: v. 知道
words.ex: I know the answer.

words.tr: adj. 搞错的；弄错的；误解的； v. “mistake”的过去分词；
words.ex: He was mistaken about the time of the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他对会议的时间搞错了。
words.en: If you are mistaken about something, you are wrong about it.

words.tr:
n. 骑；乘坐；
v. 骑；乘坐；
words.ex: He gave me a ride on his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他让我骑了他的自行车。
words.en: To sit on and control the movement of an animal, especially a horse, or to travel in or on a vehicle or other conveyance.

words.tr: v. 骑；“ride”的过去式；
words.ex: He rode a bike to school yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天骑自行车去学校。
words.en: To sit on and control the movement of an animal, especially a horse, or to travel in a vehicle, especially a bicycle or motorcycle.

words.tr: v. “ride”的过去分词； adj. 受困扰的；
words.ex: The horse has been ridden every day.
words.en: If a place or thing is ridden with something, it is full of it or dominated by it.

words.tr:
v. 给…打电话；响铃；
n. 环；环形物；铃声；拳击场；
words.ex: I will ring you tomorrow.
words.en: A ring is a small circular band, typically of precious metal and often set with one or more gemstones, worn on a finger as an ornament or a token of marriage, engagement, or authority. It can also refer to the act of making a clear resonant or vibrating sound, or to encircle or surround something.

words.tr: v. 响铃；“ring”的过去式；
words.ex: The phone rang at midnight.
words.en: To make a telephone call; to cause a bell or similar device to make a sound; to surround or encircle; a small circular band, typically of precious metal and often set with one or more gemstones, worn on a finger as an ornament or a token of marriage, engagement, or authority.

words.tr: v. 响铃；“ring”的过去分词；
words.ex: The phone rung three times before she answered.
words.ex_cn: 电话响了三声，她才接起来。
words.en: A rung is one of the horizontal supports on a ladder for a person's foot.

words.tr:
n. 上升；提高；
v. 上升；提高；
words.ex: There was a rise in temperature yesterday.
words.en: If an amount or level rises, it increases; if something rises, it moves upwards; if you rise, you stand up; if you rise, you get out of bed.

words.tr: n. 玫瑰； v. 上升；提高；“rise”的过去式；
words.ex: She picked a red rose from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她从花园里摘了一朵红玫瑰。
words.en: A rose is a flower, often with a pleasant smell, which grows on a bush with thorns on the stems.

words.tr: v. 上升；“rise”的过去分词；提高；
words.ex: The sun has risen in the east.
words.en: To have moved upwards or to have increased in level or amount.

words.tr: v. 看；领悟；
words.ex: I see a bird in the tree.
words.en: to perceive with the eyes; to understand or comprehend something

words.tr: v. 看；“see”的过去式；
words.ex: I saw a bird fly over the house.
words.ex_cn: 我看到一只鸟飞过房子。
words.en: A saw is a tool consisting of a tough blade, wire, or chain with a hard toothed edge. It is used to cut through material, very often wood, though sometimes metal or stone. The cut is made by placing the toothed edge against the material and moving it forcefully forth and less forcefully back or continuously forward.

words.tr: v. “see”的过去分词；看；领悟；
words.ex: I have seen that movie before.
words.en: If you have seen something, you have observed it through your eyes or understood it.

words.tr:
n. 摇动；颤动；
v. 摇动；颤动；
words.ex: The shake of the car made me feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的摇动让我感到恶心。
words.en: To move or cause to move with quick, short movements from side to side or up and down.

words.tr: v. 摇动；颤抖；“shake”的过去式
words.ex: He shook my hand warmly.
words.en: If you shake something, you move it quickly backwards and forwards or up and down. You can also shake a person, for example, because you are angry with them or because you want them to wake up.

words.tr: v. 摇动；“shake”的过去分词； adj. 受惊吓的；
words.ex: He was shaken by the strong wind.
words.en: If you are shaken, you are upset and unable to think calmly because of something that has happened.

words.tr:
v. 展示；表明；给...看；
n. 节目；演出；展览会；表现；
words.ex: He shows his photos to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友们展示他的照片。
words.en: To show something means to make it visible or to allow it to be seen. It can also refer to a performance or exhibition intended to entertain or educate.

words.tr: v. 显示；表现；展示；“show”的过去式；
words.ex: The graph showed the increase in temperature.
words.ex_cn: 图表显示了温度的上升。
words.en: The past tense and past participle of 'show', which means to make something visible or noticeable.

words.tr: v. 显示；表现；展示；“show”的过去分词；
words.ex: The screen shown the results clearly.
words.ex_cn: 屏幕显示了清晰的结果。
words.en: Past participle of show; to make something clear or visible to someone by looking at it or explaining it.

words.tr: v. 唱歌；演唱；
words.ex: She sings a song every morning.
words.en: To produce musical sounds with the voice, especially words with a set tune.

words.tr: v. 唱歌；演唱；“sing”的过去式
words.ex: He sang a song last night.
words.en: The past tense of 'sing', which means to make musical sounds with the voice.

words.tr: v. 唱歌；“sing”的过去分词
words.ex: He sung a song for his mother.
words.en: The past participle of 'sing', which means to make musical sounds with the voice.

words.tr: v. 讲话；发言；
words.ex: He speaks English every day.
words.en: To say words in order to express thoughts, feelings, or opinions.

words.tr: v. “speak”的过去式；
words.ex: He spoke to his friend yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天和他的朋友说了话。
words.en: A spoke is one of the rods or bars that connect the center of a wheel to its outer edge, helping to support the wheel's structure.

words.tr: adj. 口头的；口语的； v. 讲话；发言；“speak”的过去分词；
words.ex: He gave a spoken presentation instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他做了口头报告，而不是书面报告。
words.en: relating to speech; using speech rather than writing

words.tr: v. 偷；
words.ex: He stole a book from the store.
words.en: To take something that belongs to someone else without their permission and without intending to return it.

words.tr: v. 偷窃；“steal”的过去式；
words.ex: He stole a book from the store.
words.en: The past tense of steal, which means to take something that does not belong to you without permission and without intending to return it.

words.tr: adj. 被偷走的； v. 偷；“steal”的过去分词；
words.ex: The stolen bike was found near the park.
words.ex_cn: 那辆被偷的自行车在公园附近找到了。
words.en: Taken without the owner's consent; obtained by theft.

words.tr: v. 游泳
words.ex: He swims every morning.
words.en: To swim means to move through water by moving your arms and legs, without touching the bottom.

words.tr: v. 游泳；“swim”的过去式；
words.ex: He swam across the lake yesterday.
words.en: Swam is the past tense of swim, which means to move through water by moving the arms and legs.

words.tr: v. 游泳；“swim”的过去分词；
words.ex: He has swum across the lake.
words.en: Swum is the past participle of swim, which means to move through water by moving the arms and legs.

words.tr: v. 做（某个动作）；接受；带领；花费；拿；乘坐；
words.ex: He takes a deep breath before speaking.
words.ex_cn: 他在说话前深吸一口气。
words.en: To lay hold of (something) with one's hands; reach for and hold.

words.tr: v. 采取；接受；拿；取；乘坐；吃；“take”的过去式；
words.ex: He took a new approach to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他采取了一种新的方法来解决问题。
words.en: The past tense of 'take', which means to lay hold of something with one's hands; to reach for and hold.

words.tr: v. 拿；带；“take”的过去分词；
words.ex: He took the book from the table.
words.en: If something is taken, it has been removed or captured from a place or person.

words.tr: v. 扔；抛；丢；投；
words.ex: He throw the ball to his friend.
words.en: To propel something through the air with a movement of the arm and hand.

words.tr: v. 扔；“throw”的过去式；
words.ex: He threw the ball to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他把球扔给了他的朋友。
words.en: To propel something with force through the air by a movement of the arm and hand.

words.tr: v. 丢弃；抛；“throw”的过去分词；
words.ex: He threw away the old book and was thrown it into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把那本旧书丢进了垃圾桶。
words.en: If you throw something, you send it through the air using your hand or arm.

words.tr: v. 醒来；唤醒；
words.ex: He wakes up at six every morning.
words.en: To wake means to stop sleeping or to cause someone to stop sleeping. It can also refer to the trail left by a moving ship.

words.tr: v. 醒来；“wake”的过去式；
words.ex: He woke up early to catch the sunrise.
words.en: Aware of and actively attentive to important societal facts and issues (especially issues of racial and social justice).

words.tr: v. 唤醒；觉醒；“wake”的过去分词；
words.ex: The loud noise woken the baby.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音把婴儿唤醒了。
words.en: Woken is the past participle of wake, meaning to stop sleeping or to make someone stop sleeping.

words.tr:
v. 穿；戴；
n. 磨损；衣着；
words.ex: He wears a blue shirt every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都穿一件蓝色衬衫。
words.en: If you wear something such as clothes, shoes, or jewellery, you have them on your body or on part of your body.

words.tr: v. 穿；戴；“wear”的过去式；
words.ex: She wore a red dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条红色的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: The past tense of wear, meaning to have clothing, jewelry, etc., on your body.

words.tr: v. 穿；戴；“wear”的过去分词； adj. 穿坏的；用旧的；
words.ex: He wore a blue shirt to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件蓝色衬衫去上班。
words.en: If something is worn, it has been used a lot and shows signs of use.

words.tr: v. 书写；写信；写作；
words.ex: He writes a letter every day.
words.en: To write means to form letters, words, or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

words.tr: v. 写作；“write”的过去式；书写；写信；
words.ex: He wrote a letter to his friend.
words.en: The past tense of write, which means to form letters, words, or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

words.tr: v. “write”的过去分词；写作；书写； adj. 书面的；
words.ex: The letter was written by hand.
words.en: Something that is written has been recorded in writing rather than spoken.

words.tr:
v. 聊天；
n. 聊天；
words.ex: They chat every evening after dinner.
words.en: To talk in a friendly and informal way.

words.tr: 闲谈
words.ex: They chatted about the movie last night.
words.ex_cn: 他们昨晚聊了那部电影。
words.en: Talked in a casual, informal way.

words.tr: v. 剁；砍；
words.ex: He chopped the carrots into small pieces.
words.ex_cn: 他把胡萝卜剁成了小块。
words.en: To chop something means to cut it into pieces with a sharp tool such as a knife or axe. It can also refer to the act of reducing something in amount or size.

words.tr: v. 砍；大量削减（chop 的过去分词）；
words.ex: He chopped wood for the fire.
words.en: If food is chopped, it is cut into small pieces.

words.tr:
v. 落下；掉下；
n. 滴；下落；
words.ex: The apple dropped from the tree.
words.en: If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.

words.tr: v. 降低；减少；落下（ drop的过去式和过去分词 ）；
words.ex: The temperature dropped suddenly last night.
words.en: To fall or let something fall vertically.

words.tr:
v. 符合；合身；
adj. 健康的；适合的；
words.ex: This shirt fits me well.
words.en: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person's body or onto a particular object.

words.tr: v. 适应(fit的过去分词)；合适； adj. 有…设备的；合适的；按实物尺寸做的 v. 适应(fit的过去分词)；
words.ex: The shoes fitted her perfectly.
words.en: If something is fitted, it is designed to be the right size and shape for someone or something. If someone is fitted with something, it is attached to their body or made to fit onto it.

words.tr:
v. 拥抱；紧抱；抱有；挨着
n. 拥抱；搂抱
words.ex: She gave him a big hug when he arrived.
words.ex_cn: 他到达时，她给了他一个大大的拥抱。
words.en: To hug someone means to put your arms around them and hold them tightly, for example because you like them or are pleased to see them.

words.tr: v. 拥抱（hug 的过去式和过去分词）
words.ex: She hugged her brother when he came home.
words.ex_cn: 当她弟弟回家时，她抱了抱他。
words.en: Put one's arms around someone and held them closely as a sign of affection or comfort.

words.tr:
v. 点头；打盹
n. 点头
words.ex: He nodded when I asked if he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 当我问他是否累了时，他点了点头。
words.en: If you nod, you move your head downwards and upwards to show that you are answering 'yes' to a question, or to show agreement, understanding, or approval.

words.tr: v. 点头（nod 的过去式和过去分词）
words.ex: He nodded when I asked if he was okay.
words.ex_cn: 当我问他是否没事时，他点了点头。
words.en: Made a small, downward movement of the head to indicate agreement or acknowledgment.

words.tr:
n. 计划；打算；
v. 计划；打算；
words.ex: He made a plan to visit his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个去看望祖父母的计划。
words.en: A plan is a detailed proposal for doing or achieving something.

words.tr: v. 计划；“plan”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 计划了的；根据计划的；
words.ex: He planned a trip to the beach last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周计划了一次去海滩的旅行。
words.en: Something that is planned is arranged or prepared in advance.

words.tr: v. 较喜欢；更喜欢；宁愿；
words.ex: I prefer tea to coffee.
words.ex_cn: 我更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: If you prefer someone or something, you like that person or thing better than another, and so you are more likely to choose them if there is a choice.

words.tr: v. 较喜欢；更喜欢；宁愿；“prefer”的过去式或过去分词；
words.ex: She preferred tea over coffee.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: Liked or wanted more than anything else; chosen in preference to others.

words.tr: v. 提到；参考；引用；
words.ex: He didn't refer to the book during the talk.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中没有提到那本书。
words.en: If you refer to a particular subject or person, you talk about them or mention them. If you refer to someone or something as a particular thing, you use a particular word, expression, or name to mention or describe them.

words.tr: v. 参考；查阅；谈及；送交；推荐；“refer”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 援引的；
words.ex: He referred to the dictionary for the meaning.
words.ex_cn: 他参考字典查找这个词的意思。
words.en: To direct someone to a source for information; to send or direct someone to a specialist or authority for decision, information, or treatment.

words.tr:
n. 遗憾；
v. 懊悔；
words.ex: He felt a deep regret after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失去工作后感到深深的遗憾。
words.en: If you regret something that you have done, you wish that you had not done it.

words.tr: adj. 后悔的
words.ex: He regretted leaving his job too soon.
words.ex_cn: 他后悔太早辞掉了工作。
words.en: If you regret something that you have done, you wish that you had not done it.

words.tr:
n. 步；步骤；踏级；步伐；
v. 踩；踏；行走；
words.ex: He took a small step forward.
words.en: A step is an act or movement of putting one leg in front of the other in order to move forward, or a stage in a process.

words.tr: v. 举步；行走；举步，行走，跨步( step的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: He stepped gently into the room.
words.en: Having or arranged in steps; proceeding in stages.

words.tr:
n. 商店；
v. 购物；
words.ex: I bought bread from the local shop.
words.ex_cn: 我从附近的商店买了面包。
words.en: A shop is a place where goods are sold; also, to shop means to visit shops in order to buy things.

words.tr: v. 购物；逛商店
words.ex: She shopped for groceries every Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 她每个星期六都去买杂货。
words.en: The past tense and past participle of 'shop', meaning to visit one or more stores or websites to buy goods.

words.tr:
v. 停止；阻止；
n. 停止；阻止；车站；停留；
words.ex: He stopped walking when he saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到狗时，他停止了走路。
words.en: If you stop something from happening, you prevent it from happening or prevent it from continuing.

words.tr: v. 停止；停下来；停下来（stop 的过去式和过去分词）；
words.ex: He stopped his car at the red light.
words.en: If you stop something happening, or you stop something from happening, you prevent it from happening or continuing.

words.tr: n. 尖端；建议；窍门；
words.ex: The tip of the pencil broke off.
words.en: The end of a pointed or projecting object; a sum of money given to someone as a reward for their services; to give someone a small amount of money as a reward for their services.

words.tr: adj. 有尖头的；v. 倾斜；给小费
words.ex: The tipped arrow flew through the air.
words.en: adj. Having a pointed end. v. To slope or lean in a particular direction; to give a gratuity to someone for their service.
